info.title: Inbound webhooks
info.description: Inbound receiver contracts, not outgoing subscription registration. BTCPay signs exact raw bytes using HMAC-SHA256. Bank native requests use a shared header secret; Mailgun signs timestamp plus token and enforces freshness/replay checks. These are distinct authentication protocols. Acknowledgement is not proof of settlement or completed downstream processing. No Bearer authentication is used.

servers.description: Same-origin API; interactive requests disabled in the portal.

401.description: Signature, configured secret or store identity invalid

post.description: BTCPay-Sig: sha256=<lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the exact unmodified raw body>. Secret resolves from the merchant webhook secret or configured fallback; unknown store identity is rejected even with a valid fallback signature, except the separately configured subscription store which intentionally has no merchant row. Provider storeId is an upstream ID in this inbound payload only. No secret configured, missing signature, invalid signature and an unconfigured store identity all fail closed with 401. Duplicate deliveryId returns status duplicate; new accepted deliveries return received and queue work. Acknowledgement does not establish paid state.

schema.description: Recipient is mandatory. Sender fallback precedence is sender, from, From; body fallback precedence is stripped-text, body-plain, stripped-html, body-html. The first truthy value is trimmed. Normalized sender and body must be nonempty and at most 255 and 65535 characters respectively. Signature covers timestamp plus token regardless of selected email aliases.

Recipient is mandatory. Sender fallback precedence is sender, from, From; body fallback precedence is stripped-text, body-plain, stripped-html, body-html. The first truthy value is trimmed. Normalized sender and body must be nonempty and at most 255 and 65535 characters respectively. Signature covers timestamp plus token regardless of selected email aliases.

x-body-authentication.note: OpenAPI cannot express body-field security schemes. The empty security alternative means signed Mailgun body, never unauthenticated acceptance.

post.description: Two alternatives: native JSON with X-Bank-Inbound-Secret (constant-time shared-secret comparison), or Mailgun form fields. Mailgun mode is selected when recipient, stripped-text or body-plain is filled: signature is lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256(timestamp + token, Mailgun signing key), NOT raw-body HMAC. Timestamp must be numeric and within configured max age (default 300 seconds, absolute clock difference); token replay is rejected using the configured cache. Mailgun signature fields are mandatory for that alternative; no bank header is required. Both paths fail closed when their configured secret is missing. HTTP 200 only means job accepted; it does not establish a payment. SEPA automatic confirmation additionally requires observed beneficiary/credit evidence and bank-origin verification. Only an authenticated native receiving-MTA adapter may supply bank_authentication from independently verified DKIM/DMARC results; arbitrary MIME authentication headers and Mailgun delivery authentication do not prove bank origin. Incomplete or unverified SEPA notifications remain unconfirmed and require manual bank verification.

post.description: Shared Mailgun original-MIME destination for store SEPA notifications and company bank imports, including a single inbound-route configuration. Requires signed timestamp/token delivery authentication and body-mime up to 262144 bytes. Original MIME and optional envelope sender are encrypted before queueing. Server-resolved recipient ownership selects the processing policy. Stores require aligned Tatra DKIM, full body coverage and signed From/To/Subject before strict transaction parsing. Body interpretation uses either the existing fully signed MIME profile or a narrow UTF-8/plain/7bit ASCII profile whose fixed relaxed canonical wire body is bound to the same signature hashes and lengths; unsigned MIME fields never select decoding. Companies use a separate bounded MIME decoder with legacy charset and multipart support, preserving existing company import/matching behavior without granting bank-origin proof or sending a SEPA report. Invalid store proof never falls back to company decoding. Parsed Mailgun body fields and supplied authentication headers do not establish bank origin. HTTP 200 only acknowledges intake, not payment or completed import. Invalid bank proof requires review; temporary process/DNS errors retry through the queue. Configure the one shared Mailgun destination with this .mime suffix only after deploying compatible consumers and workers; no credentials belong in the URL.

body-mime.description: Original MIME form-field bytes, preserving line endings; maximum is enforced in bytes. Store verification requires UTF-8. Company MIME decoding supports bounded legacy charsets without changing the store policy.

sender.description: Optional Mailgun envelope sender. Usable nonempty UTF-8 values up to 255 bytes without CR/LF/NUL are encrypted and preferred by legacy company importing. Unusable optional metadata is ignored without rejecting the MIME delivery; companies then use MIME From. A usable sender retains precedence even when unsupported by a bank parser. Sender does not attest bank origin or change store verification policy.
